Hi Jordan & Evie —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned on the Dedicated capacity architecture work:

Notes from today:
- Goal: embed high-throughput chat and reranking workflows behind low-latency endpoints for the Acme personalization service.
- Target sustained throughput: ~600 tokens/sec (avg) with bursts to ~1.6k tokens/sec during peak campaigns.
- Typical request shape: 65% short prompts (~50 tokens), 30% medium (~200 tokens), 5% long (>1k tokens).
- Key integration items: SDK setup + auth, routing by latency vs cost tiers, structured output / tool-calling for enrichment, embeddings + reranker pipeline for candidate scoring.
- Infra asks from Acme: expected concurrency per endpoint, acceptable queueing/backpressure behavior, cold-start SLOs, and failover/regional preferences.

Redwood proposed actions / clarifications:
1) SDK & auth: we recommend initial integration using API keys scoped to the Dedicated pool; for Private/VPC we can provide service tokens / mTLS examples. We’ll include sample SDK snippets for Node/Python.
2) Routing: ability to route by policy (latency-first or cost-first). We’ll propose route configs in the sizing sheet.
3) Structured output/tool calling: we support tool-calling with explicit structured response schemas — please share an example of the enrichment flow (what tools, expected sync vs async latency).
4) Embeddings & rerankers: typical approach is to run embedding generation on Dedicated and host a lightweight reranker alongside the model if sub-ms scoring is required; otherwise use batched reranks in a separate pool.
5) Autoscaling / sizing: we discussed target throughput and concurrency. To size the Dedicated pool we need: a) QPS / token distribution (sample logs or synthetic profile), b) acceptable tail latency percentiles, c) retention/cache expectations for KV/prefix caching.

Attachments: acme-reqs-summary.pdf (your notes), and we will attach a redwood-dedicated-sizing.xlsx in the follow-up from our infra team.

Next steps (proposed):
- Jordan/Evie: share a 48–72 hour sample of traffic distribution or representative synthetic profile by Monday Aug 10.
- Redwood (Aditya/Dev/Marissa): send a completed sizing worksheet + recommended autoscale policy and queue sizing by Aug 7.
- Schedule a 60-minute architecture deep-dive (incl. infra + security) for the week of Aug 10 — propose Wed Aug 12 10:00am PT unless you prefer alternate.

If that looks right, Jordan — can you confirm the sample traffic ETA and whether procurement needs any pre-work (we can surface the contract/terms doc early)?

Thanks Marissa — this is great. A few clarifications from our side:

- Traffic sample: we can export degraded logs; expect to have a 72-hour sample by EOD Mon Aug 10. We also have a synthetic profile that mimics campaign peaks if you prefer earlier validation.
- Sustained vs burst: our sustained target is closer to 500 tokens/sec per primary region; bursts come from marketing campaigns and can spike to ~1.6k tokens/sec for ~15–30 min windows.
- Concurrency and queueing expectations: we prefer bounded queueing (max queue length per route) to avoid unbounded backpressure — our app can surface retry logic.
- Cold-start: aiming for <200ms cold-start to first-token is ideal, but we understand it varies by model/quantization.

Question for Redwood: do you have recommended concurrency per GPU for your current verified 13B and 70B-quantized profiles? Also curious how routing to a fallback model (lower-memory quantized variant) would affect tail latencies.

Jordan — thanks for the details. Quick answers and a proposed sizing sketch below. Quoting your points inline for context.

On Tue, Aug 4, 2026 at 9:20 AM Jordan Hale <jordan.hale@acme.com> wrote:
> - Sustained vs burst: our sustained target is closer to 500 tokens/sec per primary region; bursts ... to ~1.6k tokens/sec for ~15–30 min windows.

Recommended approach:
- Baseline sizing: for our verified 13B profile on A100-class hardware (typical per-token throughput), we recommend planning ~80–110 tokens/sec per GPU when optimizing for median latency with batching. For 70B-quantized profiles (int8/4) you can expect ~180–250 tokens/sec per GPU depending on sequence length and kernel selection.
- Concurrency: plan for 40–120 concurrent streams per model replica for 13B (lower if you prioritize single-token tail latency); for 70B-quantized expect lower concurrency per replica but higher throughput overall. We include concurrency knobs per replica in the sizing workbook.
- Queue sizing & backpressure: set a bounded per-route queue (we typically recommend 200–500 requests max depending on average request size) and a circuit-breaker that fails fast beyond a burst threshold. This avoids head-of-line blocking and gives predictable backpressure to the app layer.
- Autoscaling policy suggestion: hybrid policy — sustain scale by observed tokens/sec with cooldown 60–90s, and rapid scale for bursts using short-window QPS spikes with immediate extra capacity if burst > 1.5x sustained for >60s. Pre-warm replicas when possible for campaign windows.
- Routing & fallbacks: route primary traffic to the lowest-latency compatible model; on capacity shortage, automatically fallback to a quantized/compatible variant in the same region. Fallbacks will increase tail latency (we estimate +30–80ms) depending on model size and cache warmness.
- Cold-start: cold-start to first-token depends on kernel load/warm caches; with pre-warmed pools we can meet ~150–250ms for 13B.

SDK/Auth notes:
- For initial Dedicated integration use scoped API keys. For longer-term we recommend service principals with short-lived tokens (we provide the exchange flow in the SDK). We will include Node/Python code snippets and example routing config in the Drive link.

Embeddings & rerankers:
- If you need low-latency rerank (<30ms), colocate a compact reranker service (distil model) on the same pool and serve batched embeddings to a vector DB for recall. Otherwise batched rerank works well for throughput-first flows.

I attached the redwood-dedicated-sizing.xlsx with a preliminary worksheet keyed to the numbers discussed. Please review the concurrency columns and fill in your avg/95/99 latency targets and token-distribution when you send the sample logs.
